stem: The hottest planet of the solar system is –
expl: Average temperature of all planets in our Solar System is as follows – Mercury = 167º C Venus = 464º C Earth = 15º C Mars = – 65ºC Jupiter = –110º C Saturn = –140º C Uranus = –195º C Neptune = –200º C Thus, Venus is the hottest planet in our Solar System and Neptune is the coldest planet.

stem: Which planet is known as the 'Evening Star'?
expl: Venus is known as the Evening Star and also as the Morning Star while Mars is called the Red Planet, and Saturn has the lowest density among all planets (lower than water also).

stem: Which one of the following is known as 'Morning Star'?
expl: Venus is called the 'Morning Star' and 'Evening Star' as it is the brightest planet of all. Venus is also called the 'twin sister' of Earth as Venus and Earth are almost the same size and mass and have a very similar composition.

stem:
Assertion (A) : Existence of human life on Venus is highly improbable.
Reason (R) : Venus has an extremely high level of carbon dioxide in its atmosphere.
Code :

options.label: a
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: b
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: c
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: d
options.text: A is false, but R is true

expl: There is evidence of the atmosphere on Venus. The atmosphere of Venus mainly contains carbon dioxide (CO) about 96.5%. In addition to this, the surface temperature of Venus is more than 400o C. Hence due to the above reasons (CO) and high temperature, the possibility of life on Venus 2 is highly unlikely. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

stem: The planet which is called twin sister of the earth is –
expl: Venus is called the sister planet or twin planet of Earth. Venus is also known as the brightest planet, the Morning Star and the Evening Star etc.

The Magellan spacecraft was sent to Venus on a surface mapping mission. The spacecraft was launched on 04 May 1989, which arrived at Venus orbit on 10 August, 1990. It was named after Portuguese explorer of the sixteenth century, Ferdinand Magellan.
